t: Section 404(b) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (15 U.S.C. 7262(b)) is amended by inserting “, other than an issuer that is an emerging growth company (as defined in section 3 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934),” before “shall attest to”.

fable.w: This section only amends Sarbanes-Oxley section 404(b) to exempt emerging growth companies from the auditor attestation requirement. The tempting reading is that it involves private parties (issuers and auditors) and so crosses the federal boundary, but it sets up no consultation, comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue over a federal decision. It simply narrows a compliance obligation.
fable.s: other than an issuer that is an emerging growth company

opus.w: This amendment only exempts emerging growth companies from Sarbanes-Oxley's auditor attestation requirement. It sets up no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue over a federal decision. The 'attest' step is a private audit of a company's internal controls, not outsiders taking part in a federal decision.
opus.b: The likely misreading here is that the word "attest" brings in an outside party, because an outside accounting firm attests to a company's internal controls. That fails the definition. The attestation is a private audit of a company. It is not a federal decision, and nobody is consulting, commenting, or holding hearings with the government. The amendment only exempts emerging growth companies from that audit requirement.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a statute to exclude emerging growth companies from an attestation requirement. It does not establish any process for the federal government to consult or coordinate with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The attestation itself is a compliance obligation for companies, not a participatory mechanism for influencing federal policy or decisions. There is no advisory board, public comment period, or consultation requirement described in this text.
qwen_chat.s: Section 404(b) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (15 U.S.C. 7262(b)) is amended by inserting “, other than an issuer that is an emerging growth company (as defined in section 3 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934),” before “shall attest to”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text amends a section requiring attestation (which involves external auditors), it implies participation. However, the text itself only defines a scope exclusion for "emerging growth companies" and does not establish any new process for consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties. The attestation requirement itself is a regulatory compliance mechanism, not a participatory decision-making process as defined (consultation/coordination before a decision). Furthermore, the amendment merely excludes a class of entities from an existing requirement; it does not create a new avenue for outside input into a federal decision.
